Wording for an event today, tomorrow, within 7 days or more than 30 days away, and for the day after, isn't specified for this template; Part 3 R2's ladder is written for city pages (F-08).

Review notes on this page

  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: the page description (Part 5 §6's dated meta) includes '{N} employers interviewing for {role}, {role} and more.' Upcoming employer counts and job titles can't be published, and Part 5 gives no replacement for that sentence, so it shows struck through in the spec (F-03).
  • BrandonNo registration-deadline field and no per-employer interview-format field exist today; both are shown as preview data. Interview format lists only the formats chosen by this event's employers, never names or counts.
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: 'What to have ready' shows Michael's Part 5 block 9 example words where he gives them. Part 5 doesn't say what this line contains, and entry-level and diversity have no example, so a placeholder shows (F-14).
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: Part 5 gives one status example ('Wednesday 16 September, 11:00–15:00 CDT — in 10 days'), and every dated status line follows its format. Wording for an event today, tomorrow, within 7 days or more than 30 days away, and for the day after, isn't specified for this template; Part 3 R2's ladder is written for city pages (F-08).
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: the last breadcrumb reads 'Entry-Level', as in Part 5 block 1. Workstream A F4 calls it 'event', and the live Houston healthcare BreadcrumbList says 'Healthcare Job Fair' (F-11).
  • BrandonStatus, title, meta and Event markup read the same event record in the same request (Part 3 R1). The design renders as if viewed on Tuesday 15 September 2026.
  • BrandonNames come from this city's most recent past event of this type, filtered by a per-employer naming permission flag; Part 5 block 4 gives no maximum or order (F-27). Names only: Part 5 block 4 specifies 'real names'. Preview: real companies, not a record of who attended; production uses the event's own employer list.
  • MichaelPart 5 block 4 falls back first to sector descriptors. Those describe the upcoming event's employers and imply a count, which can't be published, so the design uses the second fallback: this city's last event of this type, labelled as past with the label from Michael's 14 Sep email, 'Employers who have hired here' (F-02).
  • BrandonEvent and employer job titles for upcoming events can't be published, so titles come from the jobs feed for this city and type (Part 5 block 5: 'else derived from the feed'). Titles only: 'actual job titles, not sectors'.
  • MichaelPart 5 block 5 sets a minimum ('≥4 roles') and gives no maximum and no order, so the design adds neither: every preview title shows, in preview order (F-22).
  • BrandonFeed: filter by city AND state (today the city filter also returns same-named cities in other states). Metro widening needs the city-to-metro list. No JobPosting markup: listings are aggregated click-outs, not applyable on JobFairX (Part 5 §8) (F-16).
  • BrandonLinks by slug with the event type in the anchor text (Part 3 R6, Workstream A F4). Each date comes from that type's own event record.
  • MichaelPart 5 block 7 asks for year-on-year change; the market data layer has no year-on-year field, so it is left out rather than shown as zero (F-09). Wages are annual medians as in Part 6; the data layer suggests hourly for entry-level (F-10).
  • MichaelEvery DFW satellite shows these same metro figures for this type. Part 5 §4: cap at about 70 words, label it metro-level and let the city-level blocks carry the difference.
  • BrandonLoaded on a schedule from the market data layer, never at request time. Suppress missing rows; a withheld wage shows the job count alone. Block text: 54 words.
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: Part 5 gives no preparation items and no heading for entry-level events. Block 9's fallback is 'generic prep', which his documents don't define, so a placeholder shows, with no heading, until he supplies them (F-14).
  • BrandonWritten once per event type and reused in every city; excluded from the Part 9 differentiation diff.
  • BrandonNearest 5 cities by directory coordinates that have a entry-level event, linked by slug.
  • BrandonEmployer count from the past event's registrations, never an upcoming count; suppress below the credibility floor (Part 10 ask 4) (F-18).
  • MichaelThree steps, kept short (Part 5 block 15). The journey (register, matching and screening, interview request, employer accepts or declines, accepted requests become scheduled interviews) follows the walkthrough described in the request; none of the five linked documents describes it (F-01).
  • BrandonLink text 'View employer details' comes from Workstream A F4; the href is the employer page slug, never the numeric ID (F2). Render only when F10 keeps the employer pages (Workstream C: repair, tracker S-003) and the slug returns 200 with real content, never a 302 (Part 9 check 9) (F-15).
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: block 16 gives the heading, 'tell me when the next {City} {vertical} event is announced', but no words for the email field or its button. The page shows 'Email address' and 'Email me' until Michael supplies them; Part 6's Mankato city-page button reads '[ Email me when a Mankato event is announced ]' (F-23).
  • BrandonEmail alert capture doesn't exist yet: it needs a list per city and event type.

  • Content Roadmap city row A-311, wave 3. Part 7 §2: a city's next-{vertical} pages ship in the same wave as its city page. The roadmap says wave 3, but Part 7 §2 puts every DFW satellite in wave 2 (F-13). The roadmap has no rows for event pages (F-13).
  • Type order within a wave (Part 5 §10): healthcare → technology → entry-level → veteran → diversity. This page is Healthcare, position 1.
  • Holdout (Part 7 §3): Plano is not one of the 39 holdout cities.

Review notes on this page

  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: the page description (Part 5 §6's dated meta) includes '{N} employers interviewing for {role}, {role} and more.' Upcoming employer counts and job titles can't be published, and Part 5 gives no replacement for that sentence, so it shows struck through in the spec (F-03).
  • BrandonNo registration-deadline field and no per-employer interview-format field exist today; both are shown as preview data. Interview format lists only the formats chosen by this event's employers, never names or counts.
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: 'What to have ready' shows Michael's Part 5 block 9 example words where he gives them. Part 5 doesn't say what this line contains, and entry-level and diversity have no example, so a placeholder shows (F-14).
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: Part 5 gives one status example ('Wednesday 16 September, 11:00–15:00 CDT — in 10 days'), and every dated status line follows its format. Wording for an event today, tomorrow, within 7 days or more than 30 days away, and for the day after, isn't specified for this template; Part 3 R2's ladder is written for city pages (F-08).
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: the last breadcrumb reads 'Technology', as in Part 5 block 1. Workstream A F4 calls it 'event', and the live Houston healthcare BreadcrumbList says 'Healthcare Job Fair' (F-11).
  • BrandonStatus, title, meta and Event markup read the same event record in the same request (Part 3 R1). The design renders as if viewed on Tuesday 15 September 2026.
  • BrandonNames come from this city's most recent past event of this type, filtered by a per-employer naming permission flag; Part 5 block 4 gives no maximum or order (F-27). Names only: Part 5 block 4 specifies 'real names'. Preview: real companies, not a record of who attended; production uses the event's own employer list.
  • MichaelPart 5 block 4 falls back first to sector descriptors. Those describe the upcoming event's employers and imply a count, which can't be published, so the design uses the second fallback: this city's last event of this type, labelled as past with the label from Michael's 14 Sep email, 'Employers who have hired here' (F-02).
  • BrandonEvent and employer job titles for upcoming events can't be published, so titles come from the jobs feed for this city and type (Part 5 block 5: 'else derived from the feed'). Titles only: 'actual job titles, not sectors'.
  • MichaelPart 5 block 5 sets a minimum ('≥4 roles') and gives no maximum and no order, so the design adds neither: every preview title shows, in preview order (F-22).
  • BrandonFeed: filter by city AND state (today the city filter also returns same-named cities in other states). Metro widening needs the city-to-metro list. No JobPosting markup: listings are aggregated click-outs, not applyable on JobFairX (Part 5 §8) (F-16).
  • BrandonLinks by slug with the event type in the anchor text (Part 3 R6, Workstream A F4). Each date comes from that type's own event record.
  • MichaelPart 5 block 7 asks for year-on-year change; the market data layer has no year-on-year field, so it is left out rather than shown as zero (F-09). Wages are annual medians as in Part 6; the data layer suggests hourly for entry-level (F-10).
  • MichaelEvery DFW satellite shows these same metro figures for this type. Part 5 §4: cap at about 70 words, label it metro-level and let the city-level blocks carry the difference.
  • BrandonLoaded on a schedule from the market data layer, never at request time. Suppress missing rows; a withheld wage shows the job count alone. Block text: 48 words.
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: only Michael's example items show (Part 5 block 9). The editorial content he calls for, '5 pieces, written once, reused across all cities in that vertical', isn't written, and his documents don't supply it (F-14).
  • BrandonWritten once per event type and reused in every city; excluded from the Part 9 differentiation diff.
  • BrandonNearest 5 cities by directory coordinates that have a technology event, linked by slug.
  • BrandonEmployer count from the past event's registrations, never an upcoming count; suppress below the credibility floor (Part 10 ask 4) (F-18).
  • MichaelThree steps, kept short (Part 5 block 15). The journey (register, matching and screening, interview request, employer accepts or declines, accepted requests become scheduled interviews) follows the walkthrough described in the request; none of the five linked documents describes it (F-01).
  • BrandonLink text 'View employer details' comes from Workstream A F4; the href is the employer page slug, never the numeric ID (F2). Render only when F10 keeps the employer pages (Workstream C: repair, tracker S-003) and the slug returns 200 with real content, never a 302 (Part 9 check 9) (F-15).
  • MichaelWaiting on Michael's wording: block 16 gives the heading, 'tell me when the next {City} {vertical} event is announced', but no words for the email field or its button. The page shows 'Email address' and 'Email me' until Michael supplies them; Part 6's Mankato city-page button reads '[ Email me when a Mankato event is announced ]' (F-23).

  • Content Roadmap city row A-311, wave 3. Part 7 §2: a city's next-{vertical} pages ship in the same wave as its city page. The roadmap says wave 3, but Part 7 §2 puts every DFW satellite in wave 2 (F-13). The roadmap has no rows for event pages (F-13).

Rollout and sequencing

  • Content Roadmap city row A-198, wave 3. Part 7 §2: a city's next-{vertical} pages ship in the same wave as its city page. The roadmap has no rows for event pages (F-13).
  • Type order within a wave (Part 5 §10): healthcare → technology → entry-level → veteran → diversity. This page is Entry-Level, position 3.
  • Holdout (Part 7 §3): Mankato is not one of the 39 holdout cities.
  • Workstream A first: F2/F12 (Event @id, url and mainEntityOfPage on the slug), F4 (breadcrumb and internal links), F10 (employer twin).
  • Canonical, URL and sitemap entry unchanged. Never 500, never 302 to the calendar, never an empty 200 (Part 5 §7, Part 9 check 9).
